scope.title: Wet room / level-access shower conversion
scope.description: Replace a bath with a level-access shower in a wet room: former and gully laid to falls, tanked floor and shower walls, slip-resistant floor, grab rails, WC and wall-hung basin. Structure follows one council DFG level-access specification; requirement items follow Approved Document M (M4(3) where it applies) and council OT guidance.

questions.question: Floor construction under the shower?
questions.help: Timber floors need a supported deck under the former and flexible adhesive. If unsure, the kit assumes timber.
questions.reason_upfront: A timber or concrete floor changes the former support, the deck and the adhesive class; 'don't know' maps to timber, the stricter case.

questions.question: Is this an adaptation for a disabled or older user?

options.label: Yes, an adapted wet room (Approved Document M M4(3) items)

questions.help: Adds grab rails, wall reinforcement, a curtain in place of glass and a thermostatic blending valve on the basin.
questions.reason_upfront: An adaptation switches on the Approved Document M items (rails, wall reinforcement, blending valve, curtain) and changes about a dozen lines.

questions.question: How is hot water supplied?
questions.help: This sets the shower type and the valve pressure rating. If you do not know, the kit assumes a gravity system and an electric shower, which fits any home but needs an electrician.
questions.reason_upfront: The hot-water system decides the shower type and valve pressure rating, and a wrong guess is a compliance failure; 'don't know' maps safely to an electric shower.

questions.question: Is the layout changing (new stud partition, moved fittings)?

options.label: Yes, new partition or moved fittings

questions.question: WC type?

options.label: Back-to-wall pan with a concealed cistern
Wall-hung pan on a concealed frame

questions.help: Close-coupled is the usual UK replacement. Back-to-wall and wall-hung hide the cistern and need boxing or a frame.

questions.question: Shower type?

options.label: Standard for my hot water (mixer on a combi or unvented cylinder, electric otherwise)

questions.help: An electric shower heats cold mains water, so it suits any home. A mixer needs a valve rated for the hot-water pressure.

questions.question: Electric shower rating in kW (selects the circuit lookup row; ignored for a mixer shower)?
questions.help: Match the existing circuit. 8.5 kW usually runs on 6 mm2 cable and a 40 A breaker; 9.5 kW and above usually needs 10 mm2 and 45 A. An electrician confirms.

questions.question: Main wall construction where fittings are fixed?
Pipe joint system for new pipework?
questions.help: Compression where joints stay exposed or must come apart, push-fit on concealed plastic runs; solder is the low-cost trade option.

Fit a wall-mounted fold-down shower seat?

questions.help: Sets every line that has budget, standard and premium options at once. Each line stays changeable on the review screen. Paid extras stay off.

rules.rationale: A new stud partition needs studs, plates, noggins, fixings, board, board screws, insulation, tape and jointing compound.
An installed level-access shower is step-free with the floor laid to falls towards a gully connected to the drainage, inside a tanked wet room.
Where falls are inadequate, a pumped gully and waste pump is used.
Merchants split fittings by joint technology, so the kit carries one family only.
Merchants split fittings by joint technology, so the kit carries one family only.
Merchants split fittings by joint technology, so the kit carries one family only.
Wet walls get backer board fixed with corrosion-resistant screws and washers, joints taped, then a liquid membrane kit (area / kit coverage).
Tiling needs adhesive, grout, spacers and a primed substrate.
A tiled floor needs tiles, adhesive and grout and no sheet vinyl.
Sheet vinyl is welded and sealed to sanitaryware; no floor tiles.
Walls must carry grab rails and seats (1.5 kN/m2).
A wall-fixed seat needs reinforced walls.
The LST radiator item includes TRV kit, drain-down and inhibitor.

A wall-hung WC needs a concealed frame, a flush plate and a wall-hung pan. The frames cited ship a 90 mm bend with a 90/110 mm adaptor, so a separate 110 mm pan connector is not added (this differs from the original brief). Plate must match the cistern maker and series; that compatibility is a SKU check, not encoded here.
A close-coupled suite is bought as pan, cistern, seat and lever, plus a pan connector chosen by the soil outlet and an isolating valve on the cistern feed.
A back-to-wall WC needs its pan, a concealed cistern with a flush button, a unit or boxing to hide it, a seat and an isolating valve; no frame.
A basin needs a waste (slotted or unslotted to match its overflow), a 32 mm trap with a 75 mm seal and isolating valves on its feeds.
Pedestal basin chosen.
Wall-hung basin chosen.
A wall-hung basin on a stud wall needs backing for its fixings.
A vanity basin replaces the pedestal or wall-hung basin.

An electric shower needs a dedicated circuit: 45 A double-pole isolator (3 mm gap), 30 mA RCD protection, an MCB and cable sized from the kW lookup, a mains cold feed with an isolating valve, and notification (new circuit, special location).
A bar mixer needs isolating valves close to the valve, thread sealant (not supplied) and a riser kit when not bundled; no shower circuit.
With a gravity (or unknown) hot-water system the standard shower is electric, which needs its own circuit and no hot feed.
With a combi or unvented system the standard shower is a thermostatic bar mixer; no shower circuit and no pump.
A shower pump or power shower must not be fitted to a combi boiler or an unvented cylinder.
A mixer on a gravity system needs a pump (or a low-pressure valve, which the line notes).

The fan needs a local all-pole isolator (3 mm gap), 100 mm duct, an external terminal and a condensation trap. The source asks for the trap on moisture-laden ducted air; it is always included here and can be unticked on site. Rates come from parameters, not the template.
Mira guides warn stud partitions may need alternative fixings; wall fixings are not supplied.
Wall fixings suited to the substrate are not supplied.
M4(3) basins are wall-hung; lever taps help limited grip; basin hot water is blended in the DFG spec cited.
A wet room that is not an adaptation uses a fixed glass panel; the adaptation specifications prefer a curtain.
An adapted wet room uses a curtain and rail, not glass.

finish_levels.label: Budget
finish_levels.description: The cheapest option that still meets the rules, where the research found one. Lines without a budget option keep the standard pick.

finish_levels.label: Standard
finish_levels.description: The option the research found most used, and compliant. This is the default; it is labelled 'most used' only where the evidence grade is B or better.

finish_levels.label: Premium
finish_levels.description: A higher-specification option where the research found one. Never pre-selected; paid add-ons stay off even at this level.

schema_changes: job-kit-ui/2 is additive over job-kit-ui/1: every v1 field keeps its name and meaning.
Top level: finish_levels [{id, label, description}] and schema_changes [string].
Question: help, widget (cards|segmented|toggle|select), reason_upfront, unknown {label, maps_to} (answer "unknown" resolves to maps_to) and impact (equal to priority).
Line option: evidence_grade (A-D), why_default and price_band {min, max, currency, per, vat, observed_on, basis} (prices are dated observations, not quotes).
Line: forced_by {text, source_url} (a rule fixes this line; explain it, do not offer a choice) and help.
finish_level selects on every line with options the option tagged with that level if present (the line default when it carries the tag), otherwise the line default.
